title: Evaluation of Glucocorticoids Plus Rituximab Compared to Glucocorticoids Plus Placebo for the Treatment of Patients With Newly-Diagnosed or Relapsing IgA Vasculitis (RIGA)
official: Evaluation of Glucocorticoids plus Rituximab Compared to Glucocorticoids Plus Placebo for the Treatment of Patients With Newly-Diagnosed or Relapsing IgA vasculitis: A Prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blind study
summary: Main objective: To determine the efficacy of rituximab to induce remission in patients with newly-diagnosed or relapsing adult IgAV.
conditions: Patients with a diagnosis of IgAV according to Chapel Hill Consensus Conference definitions. Patients will require having a biopsy-proven diagnosis of IgAV.

interventions.name: MabThera 500 mg concentrate for solution for infusion
Rixathon 500 mg concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Biopsy-proven diagnosis of IgAV according to Chapel Hill Consensus Conference definitions
2. Patient aged of 18 years or older
3. Patients with newly-diagnosed disease or relapsing disease at the time of screening, with an active disease defined by active manifestations attributable to IgAV
4. Patients with severe involvement of at least one organ
5. Patients within the first 21 days following initiation/increase of corticosteroids at a dose ≤1 mg/kg/day (pulses of methylprednisolone before oral corticosteroids therapy are not mandatory by the protocol but are allowed according to the physician’s discretion )
6. Patients must have signed an informed consent form prior to any study related procedures
7. Patients must be affiliated to the national health insurance
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis, or other vasculitis, defined by the ACR criteria and/or the Chapel Hill Consensus Conference
2. Patients with IgAV in remission of the disease
3. Patients with severe cardiac failure defined as class IV in New York Heart Association
4. Patients with severe, uncontrolled cardiac disease
5. Patients with acute infections or chronic active infections (including HIV, HBV or HCV)
6. Patients with active cancer or recent malignancy (<5 years), except basocellular carcinoma and prostatic cancer of low activity controlled by hormonal treatment
7. Pregnant women and breastfeeding. Patients with childbearing potential must use reliable contraceptive methods throughout the study and at least for 12 months after the last study drug administration
8. Patients with IgAV who have already been treated with rituximab within the previous 12 months
9. New onset of immunosuppressive therapy within the last 3 months
10. Patients unable to give written informed consent prior to participation in the study,
11. Being deprived of liberty or under guardianship.
12. Patients with hypersensitivity to human or chimeric monoclonal antibodies
13. Patients with contraindication to use rituximab
14. Patients treated with any concomitant drugs contraindicated for use with the rituximab according to its SmPC
15. Patients with contraindication to use routine care treatments (Glucocorticoids, Angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACEis) or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), dexchlorphéniramine)
16. Patients in a severely immunocompromised state
17. Patients with other uncontrolled diseases, including drug or alcohol abuse, severe psychiatric disorders, that could interfere with his/her compliance to the protocol requirements
18. Patients currently participating in another clinical study or 3 months prior to randomization
19. Patients suspected not to be observant to the proposed treatments
